finding.claim: /fetch2 forwards an attacker-supplied URL to requests.get with only a scheme check and redirects enabled, allowing requests to internal hosts and metadata endpoints with the response body returned to the caller.

trace.note: url read from query string, no validation
urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host/IP/redirect checks
requests.get follows redirects by default; response text[:200] returned in JSON

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist only (validators.py:6-7). No IP-range, hostname, port, or redirect validation. Redirects not disabled, so a public URL can 302 to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on the /fetch2 path is is_http_url at views.py:20, which calls validators.py:7 and tests only the scheme. Nothing checks the host or IP, and allow_redirects is left at its default (true) at views.py:22. The stronger is_safe_url IP check exists in validators.py:10-18 but /fetch2 does not call it. /fetch at views.py:12 and :14 does use it and sets allow_redirects=False, so the protection is present on /fetch and missing on /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The url comes from request.args at views.py:19 with no authentication, and views.py:20-22 pass it to requests.get after a scheme-only check (validators.py:7), with redirects enabled and the first 200 chars of the body returned, so an attacker can reach internal hosts or metadata endpoints directly or through a redirect.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the resolved IPs of the hostname, but requests.get re-resolves the hostname at connection time, so DNS rebinding can bypass the private-IP check and reach internal addresses.

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo(hostname) resolves once for the check
rejects private, loopback, link-local, reserved addresses from the first lookup
requests.get resolves hostname again; attacker DNS can return public IP first and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 second

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (validators.py:12) and resolved-IP range check (validators.py:14-17) are sound for the addresses seen at check time but not pinned to the connection. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) blocks redirect bypasses. Possible URL parser differential between urllib.parse (validators.py:3) and urllib3 inside requests was not tested. Ports: validator uses parsed.port or 443 while request uses 80 for plain http; not a bypass by itself. is_multicast and is_unspecified are not checked explicitly.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks before the sink are the scheme and hostname presence check (validators.py:12) and the resolved-IP range check (validators.py:14-17), and neither is a closing guard under the rubric: there is no exact hostname allowlist and no scheme-plus-host membership. The IP check resolves the hostname once, but requests.get at views.py:14 resolves it again at connect time, so the check does not bind the connection. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) only blocks redirect-based bypasses, not rebinding.
verdict.reason: The url comes from request.args at views.py:11 with no authentication, is_safe_url (views.py:12, validators.py:14-17) validates a single getaddrinfo result, and requests.get(url) at views.py:14 performs a fresh DNS lookup, so an attacker-controlled DNS name can return a public IP for the check and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 for the fetch. The response body is returned (views.py:14, first 200 chars), so the rebinding yields readable internal content. The same file also has /fetch2 (views.py:22) with only a scheme check, which is a more direct SSRF with no IP check at all.
